question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{12n\pi }{6} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{4n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(12n+1)\pi }{6} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(4n+1)\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{2}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{\pi }{6}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}=\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{12}.
$$
